html:
An epidemic of rinderpest, a virus that kills cattle, that swept Africa from the Horn to the Cape between 1887 and 1897. It is usually traced to infected cattle brought to Eritrea by the Italian army in 1887.

It killed most of the cattle wherever it went, sometimes nine in ten, and also buffalo, giraffe and wildebeest. For herding peoples such as the Maasai, whose food and wealth were cattle, it was a catastrophe. In Ethiopia it killed the oxen used for ploughing and helped cause the Great Ethiopian Famine.

The plague struck just as Europeans were carving up Africa, and weakened societies were less able to resist. In southern Africa its arrival in 1896 fed into the Ndebele and Shona risings against the British South Africa Company. With fewer animals grazing, bush spread, and with it the tsetse fly.

Rinderpest was declared wiped out in 2011, only the second disease ever eradicated, after smallpox.
